The harness creates a plain logfmt parser with no type table (`types_len == 0`) and passes the exact 5-byte witness directly into `flb_parser_do()`.

Source. The parser treats input byte `0xff` as an identifier byte, so `key` aliases the first testcase byte and `key_len = 1` when `c` stops at `=`. That non-empty key is the first project-materialized state that keeps this pair on the vulnerable path.

After the `=` delimiter, the quoted-value branch advances past `"`, sets `value = c`, and scans bytes `5c 30` (`\\0`). Encountering the backslash sets `value_escape = FLB_TRUE`; the loop then advances over `'0'` to `end`, so `value_len = 2` even though there is no closing quote.

Because the harness parser has `types_len == 0`, the plain string path is used. With `key_len > 0`, `value_len > 0`, and `value_escape == FLB_TRUE`, the code allocates `out_str` and calls `flb_unescape_string_utf8()` on the two-byte value slice from step 2.

On the first iteration, `in_buf` points to the backslash and `sz == 2`. `next = in_buf + 1` therefore points to the only remaining byte `'0'`. Because `*next` is not one of the explicitly handled escapes, the default branch calls `u8_read_escape_sequence()` on that one-byte suffix without supplying any remaining-length bound.

The helper receives `str` pointing at the single byte `'0'`, so the octal branch is taken. It copies that first digit into `digs[0]`, increments `dno` to 1 and `i` to 1, and has now exhausted the only valid byte in the slice.

Root cause. The continuation test still probes `str[i]` for another octal digit but the helper has no remaining-size parameter and no `i < size` guard. After step 5, `i == 1` while only one byte was valid, so this condition asks for a second digit outside the slice. The patch changes this exact test to `i < size && octal_digit(str[i]) && dno < 3` and threads `size` into the helper.
